title: GOBI 👀 - OpenAI's answer to Google Gemini?

comments.author: @cacogenicist
comments.text: It seems to me there's another, deeper sense of multimodality in which a model would be trained on text and video (etc) such that the semantic units extracted from text are mapped to objects and spatio-temporal phenomena identified in video -- where morphemes of natural language have referents. That seems a more interesting sort of multimodality.

comments.author: @frankv8858
comments.text: Yesterday I sat down for three hours and I wrote an application using HTML and JavaScript. I don't even know the first thing about how to write JavaScript. Chat gbd did it all with my prompting and explaining what I wanted. The only painful part was that I had to cut and paste what chatgpt was telling me into codepen. My next step is to figure out how to get ChatGPT to edit the code itself directly and just take my instructions. I can't imagine what a season programmer could produce in a day if they were connected to an IDE that had chat GPT connected to it. That programmer would be a thousand times more productive than he used to be. Be honest I don't even understand what the potential impact here but it's incredible.

comments.author: @DanielSeacrest
comments.text:
As of my knowledge Gobi is much more focused on multimodality, rather than other large improvements in like intelligence reasoning etc. Another model, or system, called Arrakis is much more focused on these improvements. Its much, much, smarter than GPT-4, is a great autonomous agent and is also multimodal. However im not entirely sure if OpenAI will release this model as GPT-5 (as i know they were working on autonomous agents more oriented towards helping business and government rather than individuals), but i guess we will see.

ALso there is a beta toggle called "Project Sunshine" and im pretty sure this is how you enable image generation in ChatGPT, but i think it might be possible that it when you turn it on you get access to another model which is just GPT4 with Vision, but im not entirely sure about that.
